record.original_question: Polynomially decaying eigenvalues: Fix constants $epsilon > 0$ and $p > 0$. Let $A_n C^n x n$, $n>= 1$, be a sequence of random positive definite matrices constructed via A_n = U Lambda_n U*, where U C^n x n is Haar unitary, Lambda_n = diag 1^-p, 2^-p, ..., n^-p . Let $b_n = A_n z_n$ be a sequence of random vectors where $z_n C^n$ is distributed uniformly on the sphere. What is the asymptotic behavior of $T_ CG(A_n,b_n,epsilon)$ compared with $T_ RCD(A_n,b_n,epsilon)$ as $n -> infinity$?

evidence.quote: Fix constants $\varepsilon > 0$ and $p > 0$. Let $\mathbf{A}_n \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$, $n\geq 1$, be a sequence of random positive definite matrices constructed via \begin{equation*} \mathbf{A}_n = \mathbf{U} \mathbf{\Lambda}_n \mathbf{U}^*, \quad \text{where } \begin{cases} \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n} \text{ is Haar unitary}, \\ \mathbf{\Lambda}_n = \operatorname{diag}\{1^{-p}, 2^{-p}, \ldots, n^{-p}\}. \end{cases} \end{equation*} Let $\mathbf{b}_n = \mathbf{A}_n \mathbf{z}_n$ be a sequence of random vectors where $\mathbf{z}_n \in \mathbb{C}^n$ is distributed uniformly on the sphere. What is the asymptotic behavior of $T_{\rm CG}(\mathbf{A}_n,\mathbf{b}_n,\epsilon)$ compared with $T_{\rm RCD}(\mathbf{A}_n,\mathbf{b}_n,\epsilon)$ as $n \rightarrow \infty$?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\varepsilon > 0$ and $p > 0$ be fixed constants. For each integer $n \geq 1$, define a random positive definite matrix $\mathbf{A}_n \in \mathbb{C}^{n \times n}$ by
$$\mathbf{A}_n = \mathbf{U}\,\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_n\,\mathbf{U}^*,$$
where $\mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{C}^{n\times n}$ is Haar-distributed on the unitary group $\mathrm{U}(n)$, and $\boldsymbol{\Lambda}_n = \operatorname{diag}(1^{-p}, 2^{-p}, \ldots, n^{-p})$. Let $\mathbf{z}_n \in \mathbb{C}^n$ be drawn uniformly from the unit sphere, independently of $\mathbf{U}$, and set $\mathbf{b}_n = \mathbf{A}_n \mathbf{z}_n$.

For a Hermitian positive definite $\mathbf{A}$ and right-hand side $\mathbf{b}$, let $T_{\mathrm{CG}}(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{b},\varepsilon)$ denote the smallest number of iterations $k$ such that the conjugate gradient iterate $\mathbf{x}_k$ (started from $\mathbf{x}_0 = \mathbf{0}$) applied to the linear system $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ satisfies
$$\|\mathbf{x}_k - \mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{b}\|_{\mathbf{A}} \leq \varepsilon\,\|\mathbf{A}^{-1}\mathbf{b}\|_{\mathbf{A}},$$
where $\|\mathbf{v}\|_{\mathbf{A}} = \sqrt{\mathbf{v}^*\mathbf{A}\mathbf{v}}$. Let $T_{\mathrm{RCD}}(\mathbf{A},\mathbf{b},\varepsilon)$ denote the analogous expected stopping time for the randomized coordinate descent method applied to the quadratic $\frac{1}{2}\mathbf{x}^*\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} - \Re(\mathbf{b}^*\mathbf{x})$, where at each iteration a coordinate is selected uniformly at random and the iterate is updated by exact minimization along that coordinate, with the same relative error stopping criterion.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $T_{\mathrm{CG}}(\mathbf{A}_n,\mathbf{b}_n,\varepsilon)$ as compared with $T_{\mathrm{RCD}}(\mathbf{A}_n,\mathbf{b}_n,\varepsilon)$ as $n \to \infty$ (in particular, the leading-order growth rates and their ratio, in probability or expectation).

status_evidence.title: Conjugate Gradients Acceleration of Coordinate Descent for Linear Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses how Kaczmarz/coordinate-descent iterations can be accelerated by conjugate gradient ideas, but does not address the specific Haar-unitary, polynomially decaying eigenvalue asymptotic comparison.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on CG vs CD exists but does not resolve the asymptotic comparison in this specific random model.

status_evidence.title: Coordinate-wise descent methods for leading eigenvalue problems
status_evidence.snippet: Analyzes coordinate descent methods in numerical linear algebra contexts but not the specific CG vs RCD comparison under Haar-unitary random PD matrices with polynomially decaying spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: No match found for the precise asymptotic comparison posed.
